title: Doi (identifier)
summary: A DOI is a persistent identifier standardized by ISO that uniquely identifies digital objects. It consists of a prefix identifying the registrant and a suffix chosen by the registrant to identify a specific object. The system uses a federation of registration agencies coordinated by the International DOI Foundation to assign and resolve identifiers to metadata, typically URLs, ensuring long-term actionability.

mechanisms.title: Structural composition
mechanisms.explanation: A DOI string is divided into a prefix and suffix separated by a slash. The prefix begins with "10" and includes a registrant code (e.g., 10.1000), while the suffix is assigned by the registrant to identify the specific object. This structure allows the identifier to remain fixed even if the object's location changes.

mechanisms.title: Resolution via metadata binding
mechanisms.explanation: A DOI resolves to its target object by being bound to metadata, typically a URL where the object is located. The International DOI Foundation coordinates a federation of registration agencies that manage this binding, allowing the DOI to redirect requests to the correct online location even if the URL changes.
